text.p: A confessed murderer was executed in Texas Wednesday for the 1983 shooting of a Dallas hitchhiker, prison officials said.

Kenneth Edward Gentry, 36, admitted to killing Jimmy Don Ham and dumping his body in a lake north of Dallas. At the time of the shooting, Gentry was on the run after escaping from a Georgia prison more than a year earlier, prosecutors said.
"To J.D.'s family, I'm sorry for the suffering you've been through the past 14 years. I hope you get peace tonight," Gentry said to members of the victim's family, who witnessed the execution here.

Gentry was injected with a dose of lethal chemicals and died shortly after 7 p.m. EDT, a prison spokesman said. He was the sixth person executed in Texas this year and the 113th in the state since capital punishment resumed in 1982.
